section_summaries.individual_presentation: intermittent symptoms for 22 years; progressive and fluctuating axial muscular rigidity, painful muscle spasms, and abnormal gait 17-year history of intermittent, painless extensor spasms of both legs; anxiety, left leg stiffness, exaggerated lumbar lordosis, and a hesitant gait intermittent spasms of the legs, lower part of the trunk, and left shoulder; spasms precipitated by movements of the legs in bed and attempts to walk, resulting in frequent sudden falls; extremely anxious and unwilling to leave bed due to fear of precipitating spasms; extensor spasms and tremor in both legs with attempts to arise from bed and following rectal examination; painful spasms lasting 30 to 60 seconds associated with fear and anxiety; lumbar hyperlordosis with marked hypertrophy of the paralumbar muscles; rigidity absent in supine position but hyperlordotic posture persisted; no muscle weakness or atrophy; sensation normal
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: elevated islet cell, antithyroid, and glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody levels; diabetic and hyperthyroid Brain magnetic resonance imaging, cervical myelography, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination, and thyroid function test results were normal Electromyography showed continuous firing of motor units in paralumbar muscles with the patient at rest; thyroid function studies indicated hyperthyroidism, including triiodothyronine 3
section_summaries.individual_treatment: placed on a regimen of diazepam for management of anxiety with gradual improvement in gait over several weeks treated with buspirone hydrochloride treated with diazepam, 20 mg daily, with prompt reduction in the frequency of spasms and an increased ability to stand and ambulate normally. Hyperthyroidism was treated with radioactive iodine 131. During follow-up over the next 24 months increased doses of diazepam to 60 mg daily have continued to suppress muscle spasm.
section_summaries.individual_outcome: gradual improvement in gait over several weeks; remained relatively asymptomatic until 1990 when identical symptoms reappeared treatment with buspirone hydrochloride was followed by increased symptoms prompt reduction in the frequency of spasms and an increased ability to stand and ambulate normally; continued suppression of muscle spasm with increased diazepam doses over 24 months
section_summaries.individual_limitations: The patient presented in this report was symptomatic for 22 years before the diagnosis was made She was symptomatic for 22 years before a correct diagnosis was made.
